metric: Per-query verification overhead (milliseconds beyond inference, log scale)
note: TOPLOC and DiFR overhead are author estimates from published claims; NabaOS and zkLLM overheads are primary-source figures. Output resampling overhead equals a duplicate inference run.

approaches.label: NabaOS receipts
approaches.note: HMAC-signed receipts cross-checked against every tool call in the agent loop. Sub-15 ms overhead is the fastest practical option — but it proves what the agent DID, not which model produced the reasoning.

approaches.label: TOPLOC fingerprint
approaches.note: Locality-sensitive hash of intermediate activations: 258 bytes per 32 tokens (1,000× smaller than raw embedding storage). Non-interactive — generated post-inference. Validated faster than inference ran. Hardware-agnostic across GPU types and algebraic reorderings.

approaches.label: DiFR (seed commit)
approaches.note: Verifier commits a random seed before inference; prover applies random orthogonal projections to intermediate activations. Detects 4-bit quantization in 2 tokens. Interactive: one round-trip must complete before inference can start, adding latency to every query.

approaches.label: Output resampling
approaches.note: Re-run the same prompt and compare outputs. Catches obvious model swaps but misses quantization, similar-distribution model variants, and partial context manipulation. Overhead equals one or more additional full inference runs.

approaches.label: Full ZK proof (zkLLM)
approaches.note: Zero-knowledge proof over the entire forward pass. The math guarantees every multiply-accumulate ran as claimed. Cryptographically ideal — and 3–4 orders of magnitude slower than TOPLOC for the same model-identity coverage.
